holidays.name: National Pretzel Day
holidays.description: A salty, twisty celebration of the beloved baked snack, best enjoyed with mustard, cheese dip, or by the bagful. Pretzel lovers everywhere get a license to snack guilt-free.
holidays.origin: National Pretzel Day is observed on April 26 in the United States. It was popularized in Pennsylvania, the heart of American pretzel country, where the state's pretzel bakers have long promoted the snack. Pennsylvania's governor even proclaimed the day in 2003.
holidays.funFact: Legend says pretzels were invented by European monks who shaped baked dough strips to look like arms crossed in prayer. Pennsylvania produces about 80 percent of the pretzels made in the United States.

holidays.name: Hug an Australian Day
holidays.description: A day for giving a friendly squeeze to anyone from Down Under, whether they are a mate, a coworker, or a stranger with a suspicious accent. Koalas are presumably also welcome, though they may object.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, lighthearted observance that grew out of internet holiday calendars. It plays on Australia's reputation for being friendly and laid-back, and encourages people to show appreciation for Aussie culture.
holidays.funFact: Australia is home to more kangaroos than people, with estimates putting the kangaroo population at over 40 million, compared to roughly 26 million humans.

holidays.name: Richter Scale Day
holidays.description: A shaking, rattling, and rolling day honoring the scale that measures how hard the Earth throws a tantrum. It is a great excuse to talk about earthquakes and appreciate seismologists.
holidays.origin: The day marks the birthday of Charles Francis Richter, the American seismologist born on April 26, 1900. He developed the Richter magnitude scale in 1935 with Beno Gutenberg at Caltech.
holidays.funFact: Charles Richter did not want to call it the Richter scale, and it was originally meant to measure only Southern California earthquakes. Today scientists mostly use the moment magnitude scale, though the media still say Richter.

holidays.name: Old Rhode Island Independence Day Eve Celebration of Nothing in Particular
holidays.description: Not a real holiday, but a quirky stand-in for that feeling of being excited about a day when absolutely nothing is going on. Skip it if you prefer your holidays with actual traditions.
holidays.origin: This entry is a playful invention and has no official origin.
holidays.funFact: Rhode Island is the smallest U.S. state by area, yet its official name is the longest: the State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations, which was only shortened in 2020.

holidays.name: Hug a Friend Day Adjacent: Alice in Wonderland Day Spirit
holidays.description: Fans of Lewis Carroll's whimsical tale sometimes enjoy tea parties and nonsense around this time of year. Think mad hatters, riddles, and talking rabbits.
holidays.origin: This is not an official April 26 holiday. Alice in Wonderland celebrations are usually tied to the book's July 4, 1862 boat-trip origin or to May 4, which is sometimes observed as Alice Day.
holidays.funFact: Lewis Carroll's real name was Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, and he was a mathematician who taught at Oxford.
